methodological_rigor.justification: Multi-modal preclinical PDAC study integrating human TMAs (143 UHN cohort, 54 Essen cohort, 6 Munich TMA), spatial multiplex (Phenocycler/CODEX with 27-40 markers, Opal IF), bulk and single-cell RNA-seq (GSE93326, GSE212966), CellChat cellular interaction inference, GSEA, CKP and FKPC2GP genetically engineered mice, orthotopic and PDX models, CRISPR GATA6 KO, AID-tagged degron system for inducible GATA6 degradation, and LCMV-gp33/P14 T-cell co-cultures. Mechanistic causality is established via orthogonal loss-of-function approaches (KO + degron) and rescue with combined MEKi+HDACi. Statistics use log-rank, Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon matched-pairs, Kruskal-Wallis, Spearman, and Benjamini-Hochberg correction; exact p values shown. Sample sizes for some mouse cohorts and ROIs could benefit from power calculations.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical mechanistic study (mouse models, PDX, organoid/cell line, human TMA observational correlation) maps to Oxford LoE 5 per rubric. Translational relevance is meaningful: identifies GATA6 as a state-dependent determinant of MEKi-induced MHCI upregulation and provides preclinical rationale for MEKi+HDACi (refametinib/trametinib + domatinostat/mocetinostat) combinations in PDAC, a disease with limited immunotherapy options. Path to clinic is plausible but not demonstrated in patients.

reporting_quality.justification: Animal study should follow ARRIVE guidelines; the manuscript references a Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary and describes randomization, license numbers, humane endpoints, antibody/reagent details (Supplementary Tables 2-3, Supplementary Dataset 6), genotypes, and treatment schedules. RNA-seq data are deposited in GEO (GSE146348) and public datasets referenced. Explicit ARRIVE compliance statement is not shown in the normalized text, and some inclusion/exclusion reporting (number of mice per group, blinded assessment) is distributed across methods/figures rather than centralized.

novelty_literature.justification: Establishes a new mechanistic link between GATA6-defined epithelial cell state and MEKi-induced MHCI upregulation, with EMT driving loss of the responsive population and HDACi rescuing it. Prior work (Martinelli, Brunton, O'Kane, Aiello) has implicated GATA6 in PDAC subtype and immune context, and MEKi-induced MHCI upregulation is reported in other contexts; the novel integration is dynamic cell-state plasticity connecting MEKi response, EMT, and HDACi-based reprogramming validated via AID-degron and GATA6 KO.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear abstract, logically structured methods, and detailed protocols. The study comprises multiple complex experimental modalities yet the main narrative (GATA6 -> MHCI -> CD8 cytotoxicity, rescued by MEKi+HDACi) is coherent. Some sections are dense and rely on abbreviations (CKP, FKPC2GP, AID, TIR1F74G) without a summary schematic in the text. A few typographic and incomplete sentences exist (e.g., 'Overall, the study was conducted in strict accordance with the approved animal').

key_strengths: Multi-modal integration of human TMAs, spatial multiplex, bulk/single-cell RNA-seq, GEMMs, PDX, CRISPR KO and AID-degron to establish GATA6 causality in MEKi-induced MHCI
Functional validation via LCMV-gp33/P14 T-cell co-cultures and in vivo CD8 depletion experiments
Rational combination of MEKi with HDACi (refametinib/trametinib + domatinostat/mocetinostat) rescues EMT-driven loss of responsive cell state and improves survival
Data deposition in GEO (GSE146348), compliance with animal-welfare regulations, detailed reagent tables
key_concerns: Human TMA cohorts are retrospective and small (Essen n=54, Munich TMA n=6); treatment effects in patients not tested
ARRIVE checklist not explicitly cited and blinded tumor measurement not clearly documented
Several n-values and per-group sample sizes distributed across methods/figures rather than centralized
Minor typographical and incomplete sentences in the ethics/animal section
chief_reviewer.rationale: A rigorous, multi-modal mechanistic PDAC study that causally links GATA6 cell state to MEKi-induced MHCI upregulation and provides a translationally actionable MEKi+HDACi combination rationale; tier 1 is plausible with minor reporting clarifications.
